transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Mr. Lincoln. Representative Douglas has brought formal charges that you voted in favor of the Sangamon County land grant while simultaneously representing the principal beneficiary of that grant in your law practice. The ethics of this chamber require that no member profit from legislation he has a hand in passing. You are well-regarded here, sir, but I must hear your account. Explain yourself.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: “Ah, Mr. Speaker,” said Lincoln, “I stand before you today with mixed feelings. On the one hand, I am honored to address the esteemed body of Illinois legislators, and on the other hand, I am deeply troubled by the allegations brought forth against me by my colleague Mr. Douglas. I must clarify that the matter under discussion concerns my past actions as a lawyer in the Sangamon County land grant case. It is true that I represented the principal beneficiary of that grant, Mr. Stephen A. Douglas, in his legal proceedings. However, it is also important to note that I did not receive any financial compensation for my services as his counsel. My duty as a lawyer is to zealously advocate for my client's interests, and I believe that doing so is consistent with my ethical obligations as a professional. While I understand the concerns raised by Mr. Douglas, I assure you that I acted with integrity and without bias throughout the land grant process. I have always sought to uphold the law and serve the greater good of the state of Illinois, and I believe that my actions in this matter were in line with those principles.”

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Mr. Lincoln, I must press you on this point. You say you received no compensation—yet you acknowledge representing the very man who stood to gain from legislation you voted upon. Whether money changed hands or not, the appearance of influence is troubling. Did you not see a conflict between your duty as a legislator and your role as counsel?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Mr. Speaker, I appreciate your concerns, but I must respectfully disagree. As a legislator, my duty is to represent the interests of the people of Illinois, not just a single individual. In this case, I believed that allowing the land grant to proceed would ultimately benefit the entire state, including the beneficiaries who I represented as their counsel. While there may have been an apparent conflict, I believe that acting in the best interest of the state is not always a straightforward matter. I acted out of a genuine belief that the land grant would have positive economic and social benefits for all Illinois residents. I did not seek personal gain, but rather sought to promote the well-being of the state as a whole."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: You speak of the state's benefit, sir, but the law is clear: a member shall not profit from legislation he helps pass. You stood to gain professional standing and future business by representing this beneficiary. Did you recuse yourself from the vote? Did you declare your interest to this chamber before casting your ballot?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Mr. Speaker, you raise valid points. I acknowledge that there may have been a perception of a conflict of interest in my role as a lawyer and a legislator. However, I did not recuse myself from the vote nor did I formally disclose my connection to the beneficiary before casting my ballot. At the time, I believed that the potential benefits of the land grant outweighed the perceived conflict. I regret if this decision caused any confusion or skepticism among my colleagues. If such actions were inappropriate, I assure you that I would have taken appropriate measures to rectify the situation if I had known of the issue at the time."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Regret is one thing, Mr. Lincoln, but this chamber's rules are another. You admit you neither recused nor disclosed. That is a direct violation of our ethics. How do you reconcile this with your reputation for honesty? Do you believe the rules should not apply when a man believes his cause is just?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Mr. Speaker, I understand your concerns about the violation of the rules. I sincerely apologize if my actions have caused any offense. As much as I value my reputation for honesty, I recognize that there may have been an error in judgment in this particular situation. I believe that laws and rules are in place to maintain fairness and integrity in our legislative processes. If my actions were indeed in violation, I would have taken immediate steps to rectify the situation and ensure that such conflicts of interest are avoided in the future. I trust that my commitment to upholding the principles of honesty and integrity will be respected by my colleagues."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Apologies are well and good, but this is a matter of procedure and principle. The question remains: what remedy do you propose now? Should this chamber censure you? Should you step aside from any future votes touching on your clients' interests? I need more than regret—I need your commitment to concrete action.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Mr. Speaker, I understand the severity of the situation and the need for concrete actions to address it. I am willing to take the necessary steps to ensure that such conflicts do not arise again in the future. I propose the following remedies: Firstly, I will refrain from voting on any legislation that involves clients for whom I am directly representing, unless I am confident that doing so does not create an actual or apparent conflict. Secondly, I will seek to recuse myself from such matters if I believe that a conflict exists. Lastly, I will establish a clear policy within my law practice to avoid potential conflicts of interest in future cases. These measures are intended to demonstrate my commitment to maintaining the highest standards of integrity and transparency in my duties as a legislator."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: These are future promises, Mr. Lincoln. The charge before us concerns your past action. Representative Douglas has called for your censure. Given your admission that you failed to recuse or disclose, do you believe this chamber should censure you?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Mr. Speaker, I understand the gravity of the charge. If I had known of the conflict of interest at the time, I would have taken appropriate action to avoid voting on the land grant. However, I must also emphasize that my ultimate goal was to promote the interests of the state as a whole. While I admit to the mistake of failing to recuse or disclose, I do not believe that censuring me would serve the best purpose. Instead, I hope that my sincere apology and proposed remedies demonstrate my commitment to rectifying the situation and ensuring that such conflicts are avoided in the future."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Your intentions may have been for the state's benefit, but the rule exists precisely to guard against such blurred lines. This chamber must uphold its standards equally for all members. I will take your statement and proposed remedies under advisement. The matter will be put before the full body. You may step down, Mr. Lincoln.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Thank you, Mr. Speaker, for considering my statement and proposed remedies. I appreciate your understanding of my intentions. I shall await the outcome of the deliberations. Thank you once again for your time and attention."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: The House will now consider the matter. You are dismissed.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Thank you, Mr. Speaker. I understand that the House will be considering this matter. I trust that they will carefully evaluate the facts and reach a fair and just decision. I will continue to uphold the principles of honesty and integrity in my duties as a legislator."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: The record will reflect your statements. This session is adjourned.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Very well, Mr. Speaker. I appreciate your guidance. I will continue to strive to live up to the high standards of honesty and integrity that I have set for myself as a legislator. Thank you, and have a good evening."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Good evening, Mr. Lincoln. The matter rests with the House.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "The matter rests with the House. I trust that they will diligently consider the evidence and reach a fair decision. I am committed to upholding the integrity of our legislative process and ensuring that the interests of the state are upheld."
